messages:
deploy-bot: scheduled run: migration v2026_03_21_rename_user_flags at 1769154600. auto-canary ON. :robot_face:

sujal: heads up — this migration touches users and session tables, has a backfill step. plan: 1) schema add 2) async backfill in batches 3) constraint flip.

linda: thanks. what's the batch_size and throttle? last time we saw DB lock spikes.

sujal: default batch_size=10k, sleep_ms=2000. can reduce to 2k and 5s sleep to be safer.

amanda: product ok with longer window if it avoids user impact. what's the estimated duration then?

sujal: rough calc: ~8h -> ~32h if we drop to 2k/5s. but we can limit to tenant subset (pilot) first to verify.

pierce: deploy checklist: pin migration version on deploybot so non-idempotent run is single-run. also add holdpoint after schema apply.

deploy-bot: note: pinning enabled -> pinned_version = v2026_03_21_rename_user_flags. holdpoint set: post-schema-check.

linda: ran a quick preflight against staging copy, saw lock waits on replica during the backfill when parallel_workers=4. obvious contention on user_event_idx.

eva: can we convert that part to an insert-select with LIMIT/ORDER BY id instead of parallel workers? lower lock footprint.

sujal: yes — new backfill iteration plan: use ordered windowed selects, single writer, and checkpointing. snippet: 

```sql
-- backfill loop (pseduo)
WITH to_update AS (
  SELECT id FROM users WHERE new_flag IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 2000
)
UPDATE users u SET new_flag = compute_flag(u) FROM to_update t WHERE u.id = t.id;
-- record last_id for next loop
```

linda: that should reduce index b-tree churn. also we'll set statement_timeout=120s for the backfill connection and monitor lock_waits.metric in console.

pierce: rollback plan? if we hit >1% error rate or replication lag > 30s we abort and run revert script. revert is prepared and uploaded: `revert_v2026_03_21.sql` pinned to the same deploy.

amanda: include a short blurb in release notes: "Non-destructive user flag migration. Pilot first. Rollout gated by DB metrics." Keep it high-level.

oncall-bot: ALERT: canary-run (tenant pilot) started at 1769154380. 0 errors so far.

linda: monitoring: replication lag = 3s, lock_waits spike=2 events/min, CPU 45% on primary. so far OK.

sujal: proceed to rollout wave=1 (10% tenants) at scheduled window 1769154600. I'll push the smaller batch config and enable checkpointing.

deploy-bot: rollout wave=1 started. pinned_version enforced. canary metrics exported to #deploy-metrics.

pierce: holdpoint: wait for 30min stable canary metrics (errors < 0.2%, lag < 10s). if stable, schedule wave=2 with expanded tenant set.

amanda: thumbs up from PM. add note to release notes doc: link https://redwood/release/notes/v2026_03_21 (will update post-run).

linda: tagging eng-sre to watch the window. running a quick script to mark the backfill as low-priority IO (nice level adjusted).

oncall-bot: canary complete at 1769154560. metrics: errors 0.05%, avg backfill latency per batch 1.2s, replication lag peak 6s.

sujal: ok green. moving to wave=2 in ~10m. leaving the pinned_version and holdpoint in place until wave=3 final.

pierce: final rollback reminders: keep revert script ready, do not run destructive compaction steps until post-rollout day+1.

amanda: thanks everyone. I'll draft the release note summary and share in #product-release for comms.

linda: post-mortem note: capture the decision to prefer ordered single-writer backfill over parallel workers in runbook. will add to infra runbook after this. :memo:
